scenes.tts: Chapter one followed a vesicle through three handoffs: bud, catch, fuse. But how did anyone put those handoffs in order? What can a pile of stuck cargo tell you?
scenes.visual: THE SAME WORLD as chapter 1: one yeast cell in cross-section filling about 80% of frame height, GREY ER sheets at left, dispersed GREY Golgi cisternae in the centre, the thick GREY surface arc at right, thermometer chip top-left, 'enzyme inside' gauge top-right marked 'schematic', and the three lamps 'budding', 'targeting', 'fusion' at the bottom. Open on a YELLOW vesicle with ORANGE dots doing the Golgi-to-surface trip at '25 °C' while the three lamps blink GREEN in turn (the bud, catch, fuse of chapter 1). On 'how did anyone put those handoffs in order?' the thermometer slides to RED '37 °C' and ORANGE cargo starts to pile up inside the cell; the gauge climbs. Question card above the pile: 'What does a pile tell you?'
scenes.narration: Chapter one followed a vesicle through three handoffs: bud, catch, fuse. But how did anyone put those handoffs in order? What can a pile of stuck cargo tell you?

scenes.visual: Title 'Reading Where Cargo Stops' over the dimmed cell; the piled YELLOW vesicles keep jostling so the frame never freezes.

scenes.tts: First, measure the block. Yeast secrete an enzyme called invertase. The fraction secreted is the enzyme outside the cell, divided by all of it.
scenes.visual: Pull back so the cell sits left of centre. ORANGE dots outside the surface arc drift into a bin labelled 'outside'; dots inside drift into a bin labelled 'inside'. A horizontal fraction builds on the right: 'outside' on top, 'outside + inside' underneath, with the label 'fraction secreted'. Two bars grow beside it, both marked 'schematic': 'wild type' fills most of the way up; 'sec mutant, 37 °C' stays low. No numbers on the bars.
scenes.narration: First, measure the block. Yeast secrete an enzyme called invertase. The fraction secreted is the enzyme outside the cell, divided by all of it.

scenes.tts: Is the trapped enzyme dead, or only waiting? Return the cells to twenty-five degrees, with new protein synthesis blocked. If the trapped enzyme moves outside, it was waiting to be delivered.
scenes.caption: Is the trapped enzyme dead, or only waiting? Return the cells to 25 °C, with new protein synthesis blocked. If the trapped enzyme moves outside, it was waiting to be delivered.
scenes.visual: Thermometer back to '25 °C'. A cell-wide label 'protein synthesis blocked' appears, as in chapter 1 (no X on any organelle); no new ORANGE dots form. The piled vesicles fuse with the surface one by one: the 'inside' bin empties while the 'outside' bin fills by the same amount, a GREY bracket showing the two changes are equal. Label 'deliverable, not dead' appears once the bins settle.
scenes.narration: Is the trapped enzyme dead, or only waiting? Return the cells to 25 °C, with new protein synthesis blocked. If the trapped enzyme moves outside, it was waiting to be delivered.

scenes.tts: At thirty-seven degrees, these secretion-blocked cells become dense. In nineteen eighty, Novick, Field and Schekman used that to enrich new mutants. Electron microscopy then showed what each one piled up.
scenes.caption: At 37 °C, these secretion-blocked cells become dense. In 1980, Novick, Field and Schekman used that to enrich new mutants. Electron microscopy then showed what each one piled up.
scenes.visual: Bins and bars fade. Many small yeast cell outlines incubated at '37 °C' settle down a vertical GREY tube labelled 'density gradient': secretion-blocked cells containing accumulated ORANGE cargo sink lower than normal ones and gather in a band labelled 'dense mutants'. Three cells from the band slide out and enlarge side by side as thin-section cartoons: one swollen with GREY ER sheets ('ER'), one with stacked GREY Golgi-like cisternae ('Golgi-like stacks'), one packed with small YELLOW vesicles ('vesicles').
scenes.narration: At 37 °C, these secretion-blocked cells become dense. In 1980, Novick, Field and Schekman used that to enrich new mutants. Electron microscopy then showed what each one piled up.

scenes.tts: Chapter one's rule applies here: on a linear route, cargo piles up in the last place it reached. In nineteen eighty-one, double mutants put the blocks in a broad order.
scenes.caption: Chapter one's rule applies here: on a linear route, cargo piles up in the last place it reached. In 1981, double mutants put the blocks in a broad order.
scenes.visual: The three thin-section cartoons slide onto the dashed GREY route arrow from chapter 1, ER to Golgi to surface, each sitting at its place on the route: 'ER', 'Golgi', 'vesicles'. Label 'pile = last place reached' (as in chapter 1). A small card '1981: double mutants' appears beside the arrow; no specific pair is shown.
scenes.narration: Chapter one's rule applies here: on a linear route, cargo piles up in the last place it reached. In 1981, double mutants put the blocks in a broad order.

scenes.tts: Now a harder case. An enzyme called N S F resets SNAREs at many steps along the route. Where would a heat-sensitive N S F mutant pile up its cargo?
scenes.caption: Now a harder case. An enzyme called NSF resets SNAREs at many steps along the route. Where would a heat-sensitive NSF mutant pile up its cargo?
scenes.visual: Back to the whole cell. A rounded shape outlined in TEXT colour, labelled 'NSF', appears beside a spent PURPLE SNARE bundle at the Golgi, then copies of it appear at the ER, the Golgi and the surface, one at each step. Thermometer to RED '37 °C'; every NSF shape turns RED. Question card: 'NSF fails at 37 °C. Where does cargo pile up?'
scenes.narration: Now a harder case. An enzyme called NSF resets SNAREs at many steps along the route. Where would a heat-sensitive NSF mutant pile up its cargo?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card stays. ORANGE cargo dots wait in the ER; the RED NSF shapes pulse slowly at each step.

scenes.tts: At its earliest blocked step. In classical sec eighteen experiments, E R and small E R-derived vesicles piled up, not late secretory vesicles. A pile shows where transport stops, not when or where else a protein acts.
scenes.caption: At its earliest blocked step. In classical sec18 experiments, ER and small ER-derived vesicles piled up, not late secretory vesicles. A pile shows where transport stops, not when or where else a protein acts.
scenes.visual: Label 'sec18 = yeast NSF' appears. ORANGE cargo piles up in the ER and in small YELLOW vesicles near it; no ORANGE cargo reaches the Golgi or surface, although the RED NSF shapes there are just as broken. A dimmed GREY outline of the late vesicle pile near the surface appears and is crossed out ('not here'). The card changes to 'earliest block wins'.
scenes.narration: At its earliest blocked step. In classical sec18 experiments, ER and small ER-derived vesicles piled up, not late secretory vesicles. A pile shows where transport stops, not when or where else a protein acts.

scenes.tts: Test tubes add what a pile cannot. Cell-free assays mix donor and acceptor membranes with cytosol and ATP. Then each step can be timed, removed or rebuilt.
scenes.visual: The dashed 'cell-free' outline from chapter 1 returns, now around a cartoon test tube. Into it drop, one by one, a GREY 'donor' membrane, a GREY 'acceptor' membrane, a soft cloud labelled 'cytosol' and a GOLD 'ATP' badge. YELLOW vesicles bud from the donor and drift to the acceptor; the clock dial from chapter 1, marked 'schematic', starts ticking beside the tube.
scenes.narration: Test tubes add what a pile cannot. Cell-free assays mix donor and acceptor membranes with cytosol and ATP. Then each step can be timed, removed or rebuilt.

scenes.tts: Is catching enough to fuse? Yeast H O P S is a tether that binds the Rab Y P T seven. Separate forms missing the beta propeller of Vps eleven or Vps eighteen still tethered Ypt7-bearing lipid spheres. But they failed to promote fusion.
scenes.caption: Is catching enough to fuse? Yeast HOPS is a tether that binds the Rab Ypt7. Separate forms missing the beta propeller of Vps11 or Vps18 still tethered Ypt7-bearing lipid spheres. But they failed to promote fusion.
scenes.visual: Inside the tube: two small GREY lipid spheres each carry a TEAL Rab flag with a GREEN 'GTP' badge labelled 'Ypt7'. A full TEAL tether complex labelled 'HOPS' joins them; the 'targeting' lamp lights GREEN, and PURPLE SNAREs zip so the spheres merge; 'fusion' lamp GREEN. Reset. Show two separate trials in sequence, resetting the spheres between them: a HOPS shape labelled 'Vps11 beta propeller missing', then one labelled 'Vps18 beta propeller missing'. Each joins the spheres ('targeting' GREEN), but they stay side by side and unmerged; the 'fusion' lamp turns RED. Label 'caught is not fused'.
scenes.narration: Is catching enough to fuse? Yeast HOPS is a tether that binds the Rab Ypt7. Separate forms missing the beta propeller of Vps11 or Vps18 still tethered Ypt7-bearing lipid spheres. But they failed to promote fusion.

scenes.tts: So read stuck cargo in two ways. Where cargo stops gives the order; test tubes split catch from fuse.
scenes.visual: The tube shrinks to the right; the whole cell returns at left at '25 °C' with cargo streaming ER to Golgi to surface. On 'Where cargo stops', the thermometer flicks to RED and a pile forms at one point on the route arrow, then clears. On 'test tubes split', the 'targeting' and 'fusion' lamps, which shared one RED bracket in chapter 1, separate: the bracket splits into two, one over each lamp.
scenes.narration: So read stuck cargo in two ways. Where cargo stops gives the order; test tubes split catch from fuse.

scenes.line: Where cargo stops gives the order; test tubes split catch from fuse.
